## 1. Purpose

This module evaluates three GBLUP structures under the six simulated scenarios
and the cross-validation partitions defined previously:

- **GBLUP-A:** additive genomic effect;
- **GBLUP-AD:** additive and dominance genomic effects;
- **GBLUP-ADE:** additive, dominance, and additive-by-additive epistatic genomic
  effects.

Each model is evaluated on the same 25 outer held-out splits within each
scenario. The complete workload therefore contains

\[
6 \times 3 \times 25 = 450
\]

scenario-by-model-by-split fits.

The analysis follows the same information separation used in the original
GBLUP-ADE benchmark:

- phenotype is the fitting response;
- phenotype values from the 200 outer-assessment individuals are hidden before
  fitting;
- genotypes from all 1,000 individuals are available for construction of the
  genomic relationship matrices;
- true genetic value is used only after prediction as the primary evaluation
  target.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

```

## 2. Packages and inputs

```{r packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
RUN_GBLUP <- identical(
  Sys.getenv("RUN_GBLUP", "0"),
  "1"
)

N_ITERS_SOMMER <- 50L

library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(sommer)

if (RUN_GBLUP) {
  library(foreach)
  library(doParallel)
}
```

The simulated data and the cross-validation partitions are also used by
the other simulated-data modules.

```{r inputs}
common <- readRDS(
  "output/simulated/audit/preprocessed_simulated_common.rds"
)

cv <- readRDS(
  "output/simulated/validation/simulated_cv_design.rds"
)

phenotype <- common$phenotype
true_g <- common$true_genetic_value
geno <- common$genotype_m101

ids <- seq_len(
  nrow(geno)
)

id_labels <- sprintf(
  "ID%04d",
  ids
)

rownames(geno) <- id_labels

scenario_names <- colnames(phenotype)

model_names <- c(
  "GBLUP_A",
  "GBLUP_AD",
  "GBLUP_ADE"
)

input_summary <- data.frame(
  Object = c(
    "Phenotype",
    "True genetic value",
    "Genotype",
    "Outer validation splits"
  ),
  Structure = c(
    paste(dim(phenotype), collapse = " x "),
    paste(dim(true_g), collapse = " x "),
    paste(dim(geno), collapse = " x "),
    length(cv$outer_splits)
  ),
  Role = c(
    "Response used for model fitting.",
    "Primary held-out evaluation target.",
    "Marker information used to construct the genomic relationship matrices.",
    "Common outer cross-validation partitions for all models."
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Objects entering the simulated GBLUP analysis",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The data contain 1,000 aligned individuals and six simulation scenarios. Every
outer split contains 800 analysis individuals and 200 assessment individuals.
Each individual is assessed once per repetition, giving five held-out
predictions per scenario and model across five cross-validation repetitions.

## 3. GBLUP models

### 3.1 GBLUP-A

The additive model is

\[
\mathbf{y}
=
\mathbf{1}\mu
+
\mathbf{a}
+
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon},
\]

with

\[
\mathbf{a}
\sim
N(0,\mathbf{A}\sigma_a^2).
\]

### 3.2 GBLUP-AD

The additive-dominance model is

\[
\mathbf{y}
=
\mathbf{1}\mu
+
\mathbf{a}
+
\mathbf{d}
+
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon},
\]

with

\[
\mathbf{d}
\sim
N(0,\mathbf{D}\sigma_d^2).
\]

### 3.3 GBLUP-ADE

The third structure extends GBLUP-AD with the additive-by-additive epistatic
effect:

\[
\mathbf{y}
=
\mathbf{1}\mu
+
\mathbf{a}
+
\mathbf{d}
+
\mathbf{e}
+
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon},
\]

where

\[
\mathbf{e}
\sim
N(0,\mathbf{E}\sigma_e^2).
\]

The residual term in all three models is

\[
\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}
\sim
N(0,\mathbf{I}\sigma_\varepsilon^2).
\]

### 3.4 Genomic relationship matrices

```{r relationship-matrix-roles}
relationship_matrices <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "GBLUP-A",
    "GBLUP-AD",
    "GBLUP-ADE"
  ),
  Matrices = c(
    "A",
    "A + D",
    "A + D + E"
  ),
  Genetic_effects = c(
    "Additive",
    "Additive + dominance",
    "Additive + dominance + epistasis"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

relationship_matrices |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Genomic components represented by the three GBLUP models",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Matrix A describes additive genomic covariance, D describes dominance genomic
covariance, and E represents the second-order additive-by-additive relationship
used in the ADE model. These matrices depend only on marker information and do
not use phenotype or true genetic value.

The genomic relationship matrices are derived from marker information and are common to the evaluated models and validation partitions.

```{r genomic-kernels}
if (RUN_GBLUP) {

  A_matrix <- sommer::A.mat(
    geno,
    min.MAF = 0
  )

  D_matrix <- sommer::D.mat(
    geno,
    nishio = TRUE,
    min.MAF = 0
  )

  E_matrix <- sommer::E.mat(
    geno,
    nishio = TRUE,
    type = "A#A",
    min.MAF = 0
  )

  rownames(A_matrix) <- id_labels
  colnames(A_matrix) <- id_labels

  rownames(D_matrix) <- id_labels
  colnames(D_matrix) <- id_labels

  rownames(E_matrix) <- id_labels
  colnames(E_matrix) <- id_labels

  kernel_summary <- data.frame(
    Kernel = c(
      "Additive",
      "Dominance",
      "Epistatic"
    ),
    Rows = c(
      nrow(A_matrix),
      nrow(D_matrix),
      nrow(E_matrix)
    ),
    Columns = c(
      ncol(A_matrix),
      ncol(D_matrix),
      ncol(E_matrix)
    ),
    Symmetric = c(
      isTRUE(
        all.equal(
          A_matrix,
          t(A_matrix),
          tolerance = 1e-8
        )
      ),
      isTRUE(
        all.equal(
          D_matrix,
          t(D_matrix),
          tolerance = 1e-8
        )
      ),
      isTRUE(
        all.equal(
          E_matrix,
          t(E_matrix),
          tolerance = 1e-8
        )
      )
    ),
    Finite = c(
      all(is.finite(A_matrix)),
      all(is.finite(D_matrix)),
      all(is.finite(E_matrix))
    ),
    Mean_diagonal = c(
      mean(diag(A_matrix)),
      mean(diag(D_matrix)),
      mean(diag(E_matrix))
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  dir.create(
    "output/simulated/gblup",
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )

  write.csv(
    kernel_summary,
    "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_kernel_summary.csv",
    row.names = FALSE
  )

} else {

  kernel_summary <- read.csv(
    "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_kernel_summary.csv",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
```

```{r kernel-summary}
kernel_summary[
  ,
  c(
    "Kernel",
    "Rows",
    "Columns",
    "Symmetric",
    "Finite",
    "Mean_diagonal"
  )
] |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Genomic relationship matrices used by the GBLUP models",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 4. Held-out prediction

For every scenario, model, and outer split, the 200 assessment phenotypes are
replaced by `NA` before model fitting. The fitted model then predicts those
individuals from the available genomic information.

The GEBV is stored on the original trait scale and includes the fitted
intercept together with the genomic effects represented by the corresponding
model:

\[
\widehat{\mathrm{GEBV}}_{\mathrm{A}}
=
\widehat{\mu}
+
\widehat{a},
\]

\[
\widehat{\mathrm{GEBV}}_{\mathrm{AD}}
=
\widehat{\mu}
+
\widehat{a}
+
\widehat{d},
\]

and

\[
\widehat{\mathrm{GEBV}}_{\mathrm{ADE}}
=
\widehat{\mu}
+
\widehat{a}
+
\widehat{d}
+
\widehat{e}.
\]

True genetic values are accessed only after the held-out GEBVs have been
obtained.

## 5. Model fitting

The same outer split is used by all three GBLUP structures. For one scenario
and split, the three `sommer::mmes()` specifications are:

```{r model-calls, eval=FALSE}
fit_A <- sommer::mmes(
  y ~ 1,
  random = ~
    vsm(
      ism(id),
      Gu = A_matrix
    ),
  rcov = ~ units,
  nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
  tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
  data = dat,
  verbose = FALSE,
  dateWarning = FALSE
)

fit_AD <- sommer::mmes(
  y ~ 1,
  random = ~
    vsm(
      ism(id),
      Gu = A_matrix
    ) +
    vsm(
      ism(idd),
      Gu = D_matrix
    ),
  rcov = ~ units,
  nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
  tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
  data = dat,
  verbose = FALSE,
  dateWarning = FALSE
)

fit_ADE <- sommer::mmes(
  y ~ 1,
  random = ~
    vsm(
      ism(id),
      Gu = A_matrix
    ) +
    vsm(
      ism(idd),
      Gu = D_matrix
    ) +
    vsm(
      ism(ide),
      Gu = E_matrix
    ),
  rcov = ~ units,
  nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
  tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
  data = dat,
  verbose = FALSE,
  dateWarning = FALSE
)
```

Across six scenarios and 25 outer partitions, the three GBLUP structures comprise 450 model fits.

```{r task-table}
structures <- c(
  "A",
  "AD",
  "ADE"
)

outer_meta <- unique(
  cv$outer_assignments[
    ,
    c(
      "Repetition",
      "OuterFold",
      "SplitID"
    )
  ]
)

outer_meta <- outer_meta[
  order(
    outer_meta$Repetition,
    outer_meta$OuterFold
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

task_table <- merge(
  data.frame(
    Scenario = scenario_names,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  data.frame(
    Structure = structures,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  by = NULL
)

task_table <- merge(
  task_table,
  outer_meta,
  by = NULL
)

task_table$Model <- paste0(
  "GBLUP_",
  task_table$Structure
)

task_table <- task_table[
  order(
    match(
      task_table$Scenario,
      scenario_names
    ),
    match(
      task_table$Structure,
      structures
    ),
    task_table$Repetition,
    task_table$OuterFold
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

task_table$TaskID <- paste(
  task_table$Scenario,
  task_table$Model,
  task_table$SplitID,
  sep = "_"
)

rownames(task_table) <- NULL

```

```{r fit-all-gblup-models}
if (RUN_GBLUP) {

  logical_cores <- parallel::detectCores(
    logical = TRUE
  )

  if (is.na(logical_cores)) {
    logical_cores <- 2L
  }

  default_workers <- max(
    1L,
    min(
      10L,
      floor(logical_cores / 2L),
      max(
        1L,
        logical_cores - 2L
      )
    )
  )

  requested_workers <- suppressWarnings(
    as.integer(
      Sys.getenv(
        "GBLUP_WORKERS",
        ""
      )
    )
  )

  if (
    is.na(requested_workers) ||
    requested_workers < 1L
  ) {
    N_WORKERS <- default_workers
  } else {
    N_WORKERS <- min(
      requested_workers,
      max(
        1L,
        logical_cores - 2L
      )
    )
  }

  control <- common$scenario_control

  cluster <- parallel::makeCluster(
    N_WORKERS
  )

  worker_libpaths <- .libPaths()

  parallel::clusterExport(
    cluster,
    "worker_libpaths",
    envir = environment()
  )

  parallel::clusterEvalQ(
    cluster,
    {
      .libPaths(
        worker_libpaths
      )

      library(foreach)
      library(doParallel)
      library(sommer)

      NULL
    }
  )

  doParallel::registerDoParallel(
    cluster
  )

  parallel_results <-
    foreach::foreach(
      i = seq_len(
        nrow(task_table)
      ),
      .packages = "sommer",
      .inorder = TRUE,
      .errorhandling = "stop"
    ) %dopar% {

      task <- task_table[
        i,
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]

      scenario <- task$Scenario
      structure <- task$Structure

      scenario_index <- match(
        scenario,
        scenario_names
      )

      split <- cv$outer_splits[[
        task$SplitID
      ]]

      analysis_index <- match(
        split$analysis_ids,
        ids
      )

      assessment_index <- match(
        split$assessment_ids,
        ids
      )

      phenotype_vector <- phenotype[
        ,
        scenario_index
      ]

      id_factor <- factor(
        id_labels,
        levels = id_labels
      )

      dat <- data.frame(
        y = phenotype_vector,
        id = id_factor,
        idd = id_factor,
        ide = id_factor
      )

      dat$y[
        assessment_index
      ] <- NA_real_

      fit_start <- proc.time()[[
        "elapsed"
      ]]

      if (structure == "A") {

        fit <- sommer::mmes(
          y ~ 1,
          random = ~
            vsm(
              ism(id),
              Gu = A_matrix
            ),
          rcov = ~ units,
          nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
          tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
          data = dat,
          verbose = FALSE,
          dateWarning = FALSE
        )

      } else if (structure == "AD") {

        fit <- sommer::mmes(
          y ~ 1,
          random = ~
            vsm(
              ism(id),
              Gu = A_matrix
            ) +
            vsm(
              ism(idd),
              Gu = D_matrix
            ),
          rcov = ~ units,
          nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
          tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
          data = dat,
          verbose = FALSE,
          dateWarning = FALSE
        )

      } else {

        fit <- sommer::mmes(
          y ~ 1,
          random = ~
            vsm(
              ism(id),
              Gu = A_matrix
            ) +
            vsm(
              ism(idd),
              Gu = D_matrix
            ) +
            vsm(
              ism(ide),
              Gu = E_matrix
            ),
          rcov = ~ units,
          nIters = N_ITERS_SOMMER,
          tolParConvLL = 1e-4,
          data = dat,
          verbose = FALSE,
          dateWarning = FALSE
        )
      }

      fit_seconds <-
        proc.time()[[
          "elapsed"
        ]] -
        fit_start

      prediction_start <- proc.time()[[
        "elapsed"
      ]]

      additive <- rep(
        0,
        length(ids)
      )

      dominance <- rep(
        0,
        length(ids)
      )

      epistatic <- rep(
        0,
        length(ids)
      )

      additive_effect <- as.matrix(
        fit$uList[[
          "vsm(ism(id), Gu = A_matrix)"
        ]]
      )

      additive_incidence <- model.matrix(
        ~ id - 1,
        data = dat
      )

      additive <- as.numeric(
        additive_incidence %*%
          additive_effect[
            ,
            1L,
            drop = FALSE
          ]
      )

      if (
        structure == "AD" ||
        structure == "ADE"
      ) {

        dominance_effect <- as.matrix(
          fit$uList[[
            "vsm(ism(idd), Gu = D_matrix)"
          ]]
        )

        dominance_incidence <- model.matrix(
          ~ idd - 1,
          data = dat
        )

        dominance <- as.numeric(
          dominance_incidence %*%
            dominance_effect[
              ,
              1L,
              drop = FALSE
            ]
        )
      }

      if (structure == "ADE") {

        epistatic_effect <- as.matrix(
          fit$uList[[
            "vsm(ism(ide), Gu = E_matrix)"
          ]]
        )

        epistatic_incidence <- model.matrix(
          ~ ide - 1,
          data = dat
        )

        epistatic <- as.numeric(
          epistatic_incidence %*%
            epistatic_effect[
              ,
              1L,
              drop = FALSE
            ]
        )
      }

      genomic_component <-
        additive +
        dominance +
        epistatic

      intercept <- as.numeric(
        fit$b
      )[
        1L
      ]

      gebv <-
        intercept +
        genomic_component

      predict_seconds <-
        proc.time()[[
          "elapsed"
        ]] -
        prediction_start

      observed_test <- phenotype_vector[
        assessment_index
      ]

      true_g_test <- true_g[
        assessment_index,
        scenario_index
      ]

      gebv_test <- gebv[
        assessment_index
      ]

      genetic_pearson <- cor(
        gebv_test,
        true_g_test,
        method = "pearson"
      )

      genetic_spearman <- cor(
        gebv_test,
        true_g_test,
        method = "spearman"
      )

      genetic_rmse <- sqrt(
        mean(
          (
            gebv_test -
            true_g_test
          )^2
        )
      )

      genetic_mae <- mean(
        abs(
          gebv_test -
          true_g_test
        )
      )

      genetic_bias <- mean(
        gebv_test -
          true_g_test
      )

      genetic_slope <- as.numeric(
        coef(
          lm(
            true_g_test ~ gebv_test
          )
        )[2L]
      )

      phenotype_pearson <- cor(
        gebv_test,
        observed_test,
        method = "pearson"
      )

      phenotype_spearman <- cor(
        gebv_test,
        observed_test,
        method = "spearman"
      )

      phenotype_rmse <- sqrt(
        mean(
          (
            gebv_test -
            observed_test
          )^2
        )
      )

      phenotype_mae <- mean(
        abs(
          gebv_test -
          observed_test
        )
      )

      phenotype_bias <- mean(
        gebv_test -
          observed_test
      )

      phenotype_slope <- as.numeric(
        coef(
          lm(
            observed_test ~ gebv_test
          )
        )[2L]
      )

      meta <- control[
        control$Scenario == scenario,
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]

      result_row <- data.frame(
        Dataset = "simulated",
        Scenario = scenario,
        QTL_N = meta$QTL_N,
        H2_nominal = meta$H2_nominal,
        Repetition = task$Repetition,
        Fold = task$OuterFold,
        SplitID = task$SplitID,
        TaskID = task$TaskID,
        Model = task$Model,
        Structure = structure,
        N_train = length(
          analysis_index
        ),
        N_test = length(
          assessment_index
        ),
        Genetic_Pearson =
          genetic_pearson,
        Genetic_Spearman =
          genetic_spearman,
        Genetic_RMSE =
          genetic_rmse,
        Genetic_MAE =
          genetic_mae,
        Genetic_Bias =
          genetic_bias,
        Genetic_Slope =
          genetic_slope,
        Phenotype_Pearson =
          phenotype_pearson,
        Phenotype_Spearman =
          phenotype_spearman,
        Phenotype_RMSE =
          phenotype_rmse,
        Phenotype_MAE =
          phenotype_mae,
        Phenotype_Bias =
          phenotype_bias,
        Phenotype_Slope =
          phenotype_slope,
        Fit_seconds =
          fit_seconds,
        Predict_seconds =
          predict_seconds,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )

      prediction_rows <- data.frame(
        Dataset = "simulated",
        Scenario = scenario,
        QTL_N = meta$QTL_N,
        H2_nominal = meta$H2_nominal,
        Repetition = task$Repetition,
        Fold = task$OuterFold,
        SplitID = task$SplitID,
        TaskID = task$TaskID,
        Model = task$Model,
        Structure = structure,
        ID = ids[
          assessment_index
        ],
        Observed_Phenotype =
          observed_test,
        True_Genetic_Value =
          true_g_test,
        GEBV =
          gebv_test,
        Additive_Prediction =
          additive[
            assessment_index
          ],
        Dominance_Prediction =
          dominance[
            assessment_index
          ],
        Epistatic_Prediction =
          epistatic[
            assessment_index
          ],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )

      list(
        result = result_row,
        predictions = prediction_rows
      )
    }

  parallel::stopCluster(
    cluster
  )

  result_list <- vector(
    "list",
    length(parallel_results)
  )

  prediction_list <- vector(
    "list",
    length(parallel_results)
  )

  for (
    i in
      seq_along(parallel_results)
  ) {

    result_list[[i]] <-
      parallel_results[[i]]$result

    prediction_list[[i]] <-
      parallel_results[[i]]$predictions
  }

  results <- do.call(
    rbind,
    result_list
  )

  predictions <- do.call(
    rbind,
    prediction_list
  )

  rownames(results) <- NULL
  rownames(predictions) <- NULL

  dir.create(
    "output/simulated/gblup",
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )

  saveRDS(
    results,
    "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_results.rds",
    compress = "gzip"
  )

  write.csv(
    results,
    "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_results.csv",
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  saveRDS(
    predictions,
    "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_predictions.rds",
    compress = "gzip"
  )

  write.csv(
    predictions,
    "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_predictions.csv",
    row.names = FALSE
  )

} else {

  results <- readRDS(
    "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_results.rds"
  )

}
```

```{r task-summary}
results$Model <- factor(
  results$Model,
  levels = model_names
)


task_summary <- as.data.frame(
  table(
    results$Scenario,
    results$Model
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

names(task_summary) <- c(
  "Scenario",
  "Model",
  "Fits"
)

task_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Number of outer GBLUP fits by scenario and model",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 6. Evaluation metrics

The **true genetic value** is the primary target because it is known in the
simulation and directly measures recovery of the simulated genetic signal.

The **phenotype** is retained as a secondary target because it includes the
genetic signal together with residual variation.

Held-out predictive performance is summarized using the following metrics:

- **Pearson correlation:** linear association between GEBV and the target;
- **Spearman correlation:** rank association between GEBV and the target;
- **RMSE:** prediction error on the original scale;
- **MAE:** mean absolute prediction error on the original scale.

Bias and calibration slope are complementary measures. Bias is
`mean(prediction - target)`, and calibration slope is the coefficient of
prediction in `lm(target ~ prediction)`. R-squared is not used.

No evaluation target is used during model fitting.

## 7. Predictive performance

### 7.1 True genetic value

```{r genetic-performance-summary}
genetic_performance <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    Genetic_Pearson,
    Genetic_Spearman,
    Genetic_RMSE,
    Genetic_MAE,
    Genetic_Bias,
    Genetic_Slope
  ) ~ Scenario + Model,
  data = results,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

genetic_performance <- genetic_performance[
  order(
    match(
      genetic_performance$Scenario,
      scenario_names
    ),
    match(
      as.character(
        genetic_performance$Model
      ),
      model_names
    )
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

genetic_performance |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Primary evaluation against true genetic value",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The scenario sequence represents the predefined simulation settings. Because
the simulation factors change jointly across scenarios, differences among C1-C6
should be interpreted as differences among the complete scenarios rather than
as isolated effects of one parameter.

### 7.2 Phenotype

```{r phenotype-performance-summary}
phenotype_performance <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    Phenotype_Pearson,
    Phenotype_Spearman,
    Phenotype_RMSE,
    Phenotype_MAE,
    Phenotype_Bias,
    Phenotype_Slope
  ) ~ Scenario + Model,
  data = results,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

phenotype_performance <- phenotype_performance[
  order(
    match(
      phenotype_performance$Scenario,
      scenario_names
    ),
    match(
      as.character(
        phenotype_performance$Model
      ),
      model_names
    )
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

phenotype_performance |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Secondary evaluation against phenotype",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

### 7.3 Performance across outer splits

```{r genetic-correlation-figure, fig.cap="Held-out Pearson correlation between GEBV and true genetic value across the 25 outer splits for GBLUP-A, GBLUP-AD, and GBLUP-ADE."}
p_genetic_correlation <- ggplot(
  results,
  aes(
    x = Scenario,
    y = Genetic_Pearson,
    fill = Model
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.72,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.75,
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.8
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_gdocs(
    labels = c(
      "GBLUP-A",
      "GBLUP-AD",
      "GBLUP-ADE"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Simulation scenario",
    y = "Pearson correlation with true genetic value",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gdocs()

print(
  p_genetic_correlation
)
```

```{r save-genetic-correlation-tiff, include=FALSE}
ggsave(
  "output/simulated/m03/figures/gblup_genetic_correlation_by_scenario.tiff",
  plot = p_genetic_correlation,
  device = "tiff",
  width = 8.5,
  height = 5.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

```{r genetic-rmse-figure, fig.cap="Held-out RMSE for true genetic value across the 25 outer splits for GBLUP-A, GBLUP-AD, and GBLUP-ADE."}
p_genetic_rmse <- ggplot(
  results,
  aes(
    x = Scenario,
    y = Genetic_RMSE,
    fill = Model
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.72,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.75,
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.8
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_gdocs(
    labels = c(
      "GBLUP-A",
      "GBLUP-AD",
      "GBLUP-ADE"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Simulation scenario",
    y = "RMSE for true genetic value",

  ) +
  theme_gdocs()

print(
  p_genetic_rmse
)
```

```{r save-genetic-rmse-tiff, include=FALSE}
ggsave(
  "output/simulated/m03/figures/gblup_genetic_rmse_by_scenario.tiff",
  plot = p_genetic_rmse,
  device = "tiff",
  width = 8.5,
  height = 5.5,

  dpi = 300,

```

The boxplots summarize variation among the 25 held-out splits. They are
descriptive summaries of repeated cross-validation and are not treated as
independent inferential replicates.

## 8. Split-level variability

The same split-level results can be summarized numerically without introducing
additional model-selection criteria.

```{r split-summary}
split_summary <- data.frame(
  Scenario = character(0),
  Model = character(0),
  N = integer(0),
  Pearson_mean = numeric(0),
  Pearson_sd = numeric(0),
  Pearson_min = numeric(0),
  Pearson_max = numeric(0),
  Spearman_mean = numeric(0),
  Spearman_sd = numeric(0),
  RMSE_mean = numeric(0),
  RMSE_sd = numeric(0),
  MAE_mean = numeric(0),
  MAE_sd = numeric(0),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (
  scenario in
    scenario_names
) {

  for (
    model_name in
      model_names
  ) {

    x <- results[
      results$Scenario == scenario &
        as.character(
          results$Model
        ) == model_name,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    split_summary <- rbind(
      split_summary,
      data.frame(
        Scenario = scenario,
        Model = model_name,
        N = nrow(x),
        Pearson_mean = mean(
          x$Genetic_Pearson,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Pearson_sd = sd(
          x$Genetic_Pearson,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Pearson_min = min(
          x$Genetic_Pearson,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Pearson_max = max(
          x$Genetic_Pearson,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Spearman_mean = mean(
          x$Genetic_Spearman,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        Spearman_sd = sd(
          x$Genetic_Spearman,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        RMSE_mean = mean(
          x$Genetic_RMSE,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        RMSE_sd = sd(
          x$Genetic_RMSE,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        MAE_mean = mean(
          x$Genetic_MAE,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        MAE_sd = sd(
          x$Genetic_MAE,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
}

split_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "True genetic-value prediction across outer splits",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

## 9. Computational time

The genomic matrices are constructed once and reused across the complete
analysis. Model fitting is repeated for each scenario, model, and outer split.
The table below summarizes the mean fitting and prediction time per model.

```{r time-summary}
time_summary <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    Fit_seconds,
    Predict_seconds
  ) ~ Model,
  data = results,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

time_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Mean computational time per GBLUP fit",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )


```

These times describe the completed computation on the machine used for the
analysis and should not be interpreted as hardware-independent characteristics
of the models.
